T14: what to hold in the OUT-SELL regime (the three-index switch OUT and MAUc1 SELL)

Test T14, run headline; pre-registration sha256 99fe0f3a8c8b7d4d (match with the T14.md header: True); windows W1 and W2 with their own dates throughout; METHODS.md beside this page. Contents: answer, data, one backtest, headline, D-table, curves, R6, robustness, power, definitions.

1. The answer

Question. In the weeks when the three-index switch is OUT and the MAUc1 gold signal is SELL (the OUT-SELL regime), does holding half the parent plus half GOLDBEES (-half) or only the liquid ETF (-liq) instead of the original sleeve change what the switch earns, on both base sleeves (50/50 and 80/20), on W1 and W2? Descriptive first (the difference from the original rule, R6), then against chance (E1, E2 against random in-or-out timing; G1, G2 against random gold timing).

Status. T14, a post-hoc variant on two windows that were seen before the variants were proposed: any finding is PROVISIONAL at most; there is no hold-out. Cost 20.8 bps, LBES cash. The verdicts below are the pre-registered mechanical outcome map (T14.md 2.4); the interpretation is in the write-up (T14.md 5-8).

R6 is shown against F1 and against F3. A difference of CAGR in pp; percentile in points.

formula: e_gw

9. Definitions (every statistic once, in full)

nav

NAV_t = cash_t + Σ_i units_i × close_i,t (cash = LBES units × LBES level; GOLDBEES units × its close); base 1.0 at the close of the first session; daily marks on the window's sessions

cost

traded = Σ over every line |target value − held value| at the trade session's prices; cost = traded × cost_bps ÷ 2 ÷ 10,000 (10.4 bps a side at 20.8 bps; 0 and 50 bps as robustness); every target is then scaled by (V − cost) ÷ V

e_gw

regime at a decision: IN = all three index SIGNs BUY; OUT-BUY = not IN and MAUc1 SIGN BUY; OUT-SELL = not IN and MAUc1 SIGN SELL. target (e, gw): e = parent share of the book, gw = GOLDBEES share of the non-parent part (the rest is the LBES liquid ETF) 50-orig: IN (1, ·), else (0, 0.5); 50-half: OUT-SELL (0.5, 1.0); 50-liq: OUT-SELL (0, 0); 80-orig: OUT-BUY (0, 0.8), OUT-SELL (0, 0.2); 80-half / 80-liq: as 50-half / 50-liq, OUT-BUY (0, 0.8)

cagr

CAGR = NAV_end ^ (252 ÷ (sessions − 1)) − 1 (sessions = the window's trading sessions; years = (sessions − 1) ÷ 252; arithmetic, price return, after the stated cost)

maxdd

max drawdown = min over t of ( NAV_t ÷ max(NAV_s, s ≤ t) − 1 ) (negative; 'shallower' = closer to 0)

calmar

Calmar = CAGR ÷ |max drawdown|

vol

volatility = standard deviation of the daily NAV returns × √252 (Ulcer index, days ≥ 10% under peak and longest time under water as in T08/T11)

cmix

constant mix at a rule's own averages: f = mean of e over the decisions, gw_bar = Σ (1 − e) gw ÷ Σ (1 − e); rebalanced at every decision and every basket change

d

difference from the original = statistic(variant) − statistic(original) on the same window, cost and cash; CAGR, volatility in pp; max drawdown in pp (positive = shallower)

pct

percentile = (draws worse + 0.5 × draws tied) ÷ draws × 100, ties equal within a relative 1e-12; 'worse' = lower CAGR, deeper (more negative) max drawdown; 2,000 draws per book, cost, rule and null

pval

p = (1 + draws at least as good (better or tied)) ÷ (draws + 1)

mde

MDE = 2.8 × the SD of the null's statistic (CAGR or max drawdown), in pp; printed beside every FAIL: 'undetectable below the MDE', never 'no effect'

holm

Holm step-down adjusted p: sort the 16 p-values of a window (per book) ascending, p_adj(i) = max over j ≤ i of min(1, (16 − j + 1) × p_(j))

r6

R6: Δ_d = statistic(variant, draw d) − statistic(its original, the same draw d), for every F1 and every F3 draw (CAGR and max drawdown; positive = better); the real Δ (variant − original on the real series) is ranked among the Δ_d with the percentile formula

ledger

ledger return of a rule over an OUT-SELL spell = NAV_end ÷ NAV_start − 1 from the close of the spell's first decision's session to the close of the session of the decision that ends it (or the last session); parent = hold_parent (0 bps); GOLDBEES, cash = close ÷ close − 1
